title: Razer Soma gaming chair: Pro and Sensa HD haptics
description: The Razer Soma gaming chair range adds the Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics, with six haptic motors that let you feel explosions and impacts.
tags: Razer Soma Pro price in India

body.text: The Razer Soma gaming chair lineup has grown with two new models, the Soma Pro and the Soma Sensa HD Haptics, which Razer announced on November 13, according to Dexerto. Both use built-in haptic motors so players can physically feel explosions, impacts and approaching threats. For anyone building a high-end setup, or a cafe owner eyeing premium seating, this pushes the chair from comfort gear into part of the gameplay itself.
How the Razer Soma gaming chair haptics work

Each chair has six haptic motor actuators powered by Razer Sensa HD Haptics. Dexerto says the vibrations respond to the intensity, direction and distance of supported in-game events. Razer's example is telling an explosion on your left apart from an impact happening close by.
The tech is not limited to games built for it. Through Razer Synapse, audio can be converted into vibrations, so unsupported games, movies and music can also trigger feedback.

Players can change vibration intensity, switch profiles and manage wireless connections from a control panel built into the chair. Both models support Razer HyperSpeed Wireless for PC and Bluetooth LE for compatible mobile devices.
Soma Pro vs Soma Sensa HD Haptics
The Soma Sensa HD Haptics is the feedback-focused option. The Soma Pro combines haptics, lighting and audio in a single chair.

items: Soma Pro adds speakers with THX Spatial Audio, which can work alone or alongside front speakers for a wider surround setup.
Soma Pro also has Razer Chroma RGB lighting that reacts to events across more than 300 integrated games and syncs with other compatible Razer devices through Synapse.
Soma Pro adds 4D adjustable armrests, a magnetic head cushion and a tilt mechanism.
Both share a built-in lumbar arch, dual-density cold-cured foam cushioning and a backrest that reclines up to 132 degrees.

body.text: Both build on the earlier Soma Chroma, which brought reactive RGB lighting to the range. The new chairs add physical feedback on top, and the Soma Pro is the more advanced of the two.
Razer designed both chairs to run without a permanent cable to a wall outlet. You can power them from a compatible USB-C power bank or plug into a wall outlet for continuous use.

Dexerto's report does not mention pricing, a release date or availability in India, so a Razer Soma Pro price in India is not confirmed yet. Treat any figures you see before an official listing as unverified.

The big open questions are price, release timing and whether Razer brings the chairs to India. Also watch how many games support the haptics natively, and how convincing the audio-to-vibration conversion feels in competitive shooters. Hands-on reviews should show whether the feedback adds to your game sense or just adds noise.

faqs.q: What are the new Razer Soma gaming chairs?
faqs.a: According to Dexerto, Razer announced the Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics on November 13. Both use six built-in haptic motors to turn in-game events like explosions and impacts into physical vibrations.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Razer Soma Pro and Soma Sensa HD Haptics?
faqs.a: Both have the same haptic motors, but the Soma Pro also adds speakers with THX Spatial Audio and Razer Chroma RGB lighting that reacts to events in more than 300 games. The Soma Sensa HD Haptics focuses on physical feedback.

faqs.q: Do the Razer Soma chairs work with games that don't support haptics?
faqs.a: Yes. Dexerto reports that Razer Synapse can convert audio into vibrations, so the chairs can give feedback in unsupported games, movies and music.
